title: Syntax error
description: The source cannot be parsed at this token. This is the generic syntax error, reported when no more specific one applies.

title: Missing element
description: A required element is missing. The message names it.
sources:
NAMESPACE
END_NAMESPACE

title: Missing variable type
description: A variable declaration has no type.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Unexpected variable initialization
description: An initial value is not allowed in this section. A VAR_IN_OUT is bound to the caller's variable at each call, so it has nothing of its own to initialize.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR_IN_OUT
    x : INT := 5;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Empty right-hand side of assignment
description: The assignment has no value on its right-hand side.

title: Invalid assignment sign '='
description: An assignment is written `:=`, not `=`.

title: Invalid assignment sign ':'
description: An assignment is written `:=`, not `:`.

title: Invalid assignment sign '=>' in assignment
description:
An assignment is written `:=`, not `=>`.

`=>` binds an output in a call.

title: Invalid assignment sign '=' in FOR list
description: A FOR loop sets its counter with `:=`, not `=`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    i: INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i = 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Invalid assignment sign ':' in FOR list
description: A FOR loop sets its counter with `:=`, not `:`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    i: INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i : 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Invalid assignment sign '=>' in FOR list
description: A FOR loop sets its counter with `:=`, not `=>`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    i: INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i => 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Assignment sign ':=' in a condition
description: `:=` is only accepted in an assignment, while `=` is reserved for a comparison.

title: Assignment to a function call
description: A function call is a value, not a place that can be assigned to.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1 : INT END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    fn1() := 5;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Incomplete edge qualifier
description:
An edge qualifier is started and not completed: `R_` or `F_ED`.

Write `R_EDGE` or `F_EDGE`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR_INPUT
    x : BOOL R_ED;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: THIS after a dot in a path
description:
`THIS` can only start a path, as in `THIS.member` or `THIS^.member`, never follow a dot.

In a FUNCTION, which has no instance, `THIS` is E1105.

title: SUPER after a dot in a path
description:
`SUPER` can only start a path, as in `SUPER.m()`: `THIS.SUPER.m()` and `inst.SUPER.x` are refused.

Without an EXTENDS clause the error is E1107, and in a FUNCTION or a PROGRAM it is E1106.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
METHOD m
END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
    THIS.SUPER.m();
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR not allowed in this context
description: `VAR` declares the variables of a FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK, PROGRAM, CLASS or METHOD. A CONFIGURATION keeps its data in `VAR_GLOBAL` instead.
sources:
CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    VAR

    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: VAR_IN_OUT not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_IN_OUT` declares a parameter of a FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK, PROGRAM or METHOD, or of a METHOD prototype in an INTERFACE. A CLASS has no body and a CONFIGURATION no call to pass one to.
sources:
CLASS c1
    VAR_IN_OUT

    END_VAR
END_CLASS

title: VAR_TEMP not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_TEMP` declares the per-call variables of a FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK, PROGRAM or METHOD. A CLASS, an INTERFACE prototype and a CONFIGURATION have no code to run, so they have no use for one.
sources:
CLASS c1
    VAR_TEMP

    END_VAR
END_CLASS

title: VAR_EXTERNAL not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_EXTERNAL` imports a global into a FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK, PROGRAM, CLASS or METHOD. A METHOD prototype in an INTERFACE has no body to read it, and a CONFIGURATION declares the globals themselves.
sources:
INTERFACE in
    METHOD m
        VAR_EXTERNAL

        END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

title: VAR_GLOBAL not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_GLOBAL` is declared in a CONFIGURATION. A POU reaches a global through `VAR_EXTERNAL`, and a RESOURCE holds no variables of its own.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    VAR_GLOBAL

    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR_ACCESS not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_ACCESS` declares access paths in a PROGRAM or a CONFIGURATION, not in a FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK, CLASS or METHOD.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    VAR_ACCESS

    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR_CONFIG not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_CONFIG` is declared in a CONFIGURATION.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    VAR_CONFIG

    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: PROGRAM in a NAMESPACE
description: A PROGRAM cannot be declared inside a NAMESPACE.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    PROGRAM p1
    END_PROGRAM
END_NAMESPACE

title: CONFIGURATION in a NAMESPACE
description: A CONFIGURATION cannot be declared inside a NAMESPACE.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    CONFIGURATION c1
    END_CONFIGURATION
END_NAMESPACE

title: Variables after methods in a FUNCTION_BLOCK
description: In a FUNCTION_BLOCK, the variable sections come before the methods.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    VAR
        x: INT;
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Variables after methods in a CLASS
description: In a CLASS, the variable sections come before the methods.
sources:
CLASS c1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    VAR
        x: INT;
    END_VAR
END_CLASS

title: METHOD declared in a body
description: A METHOD cannot be declared among the statements of a body. Declare it at the top level of the FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x: INT;
END_VAR
    x := 1;
    METHOD m1
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Variadic parameter outside a FUNCTION or METHOD
description:
Only a FUNCTION or METHOD, compiled once per argument count, takes a variadic parameter.

A PROGRAM or a FUNCTION_BLOCK is an instance: its inputs are members, each with one value.
sources:
PROGRAM Main
    VAR_INPUT
        values : INT...;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Duplicate variable
description: Two variables in the same scope have the same name.

title: Duplicate POU
description: Two POUs (functions, function blocks, classes, etc.) have the same name.

title: Duplicate parameter
description: A function call passes the same parameter twice.

title: Duplicate struct field
description: Two fields in a STRUCT have the same name.

title: Duplicate enum variant
description: Two variants in an ENUM have the same name.
sources:
TYPE e1 : (Red, Green, Red)
END_TYPE

title: Duplicate field in an initializer
description: A struct initializer assigns the same field twice.

title: Return value declared again
description:
In a FUNCTION, or a METHOD with a return type, the POU's own name is its return value.

A variable of that name, in any letter case, declares it a second time.

title: Duplicate method declaration
description: Two methods in the same POU have the same name.
sources:
CLASS c1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Duplicate method prototype
description: Two method prototypes in an interface have the same name.
sources:
INTERFACE i1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

title: Duplicate inherited method
description: Two interfaces implemented by the same POU define a method with the same name.
sources:
INTERFACE i1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

INTERFACE i2
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS c1 IMPLEMENTS i1, i2
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Duplicate USING
description: The same namespace is imported twice with `USING`.

title: Duplicate PROGRAM
description: Two PROGRAM declarations have the same name.
sources:
PROGRAM p1
END_PROGRAM

PROGRAM p1
END_PROGRAM

title: Duplicate PROGRAM instance
description: Two PROGRAM instances in the same configuration have the same name.

title: Duplicate TASK
description: Two TASKs in the same configuration have the same name.

title: Duplicate RESOURCE
description: Two RESOURCE blocks in the same configuration have the same name.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(PRIORITY := 1);
    END_RESOURCE
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task2(PRIORITY := 1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unknown name
description: The name does not exist in the current scope.

title: Unknown field
description: The type has no field with the given name.

title: Unknown name in a namespace
description: The item does not exist in the namespace path.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    FUNCTION fn1 : INT
        fn1 := 0;
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ns1.unknown;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Unknown namespace in USING
description: The namespace referenced in a `USING` directive does not exist.

title: Ambiguous name
description: Several items of this name are in scope, and the compiler cannot tell which one is meant. Qualify the name.

title: VAR_EXTERNAL without a VAR_GLOBAL
description: A `VAR_EXTERNAL` names a global that no `VAR_GLOBAL` declares.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
VAR_EXTERNAL
    missing_global : INT;
END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH task1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: VAR_EXTERNAL type mismatch
description: A VAR_EXTERNAL repeats the type of its VAR_GLOBAL exactly, subrange included. A wider type would bypass the global's range check.
sources:
TYPE Small : INT (0..10); END_TYPE

PROGRAM MyProg
    VAR_EXTERNAL
        g : INT;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    VAR_GLOBAL
        g : Small;
    END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : MyProg;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: RETAIN in a stateless POU
description: RETAIN and NON_RETAIN apply to instance storage. A FUNCTION or METHOD has none, since its variables live for one call only.
sources:
FUNCTION f1 : INT
VAR_OUTPUT RETAIN q : INT; END_VAR
    f1 := 1;
END_FUNCTION

title: Variable out of reach
description:
A variable is named where its storage is not.

A `VAR_TEMP` lives while its own body runs. A METHOD of the block, a derived block, an instance (`f.tmp`) and `THIS^` cannot name it: give the METHOD or the derived block a `VAR_TEMP` of its own.

A `VAR_EXTERNAL` names a global that no instance holds, so `f.g` names nothing. Name the global itself.

A METHOD's variables live while it runs, so `f.M.x` names nothing either.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Fb
VAR_TEMP scratch : INT; END_VAR
    METHOD Peek : INT
        Peek := scratch;
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Type mismatch
description: The types on both sides of an assignment or expression are incompatible.

title: Types not comparable
description:
The two sides of a comparison have types that do not convert to each other: an INT and a STRING, a TIME and an INT.

A type with no comparison at all, such as a STRUCT under `=`, is E0305.

title: Types not addable
description: The two types cannot be used with addition or subtraction operators.

title: Types not multiplicable
description: The two types cannot be used with multiplication or division operators.

title: Operator not supported by the type
description:
The type has no such operator: `+` or `-` on a BOOL, `=` on a STRUCT, an ARRAY or an instance.

Two types that each have the operator but do not convert to each other are E0302.

title: Literal out of range
description:
The literal is well-formed but outside what the type holds. A note gives the type's bounds.

A radix literal (`2#`, `8#`, `16#`) is a bit pattern of the type's width: `SINT#16#FF` is -1, and `SINT#16#1FF` has one bit too many.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    test: INT := 32768;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Negative literal for an unsigned type
description:
A minus sign on a literal whose type has no negative values.

Use the signed type of the same width, or drop the sign.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    test: UINT := -1;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Literal of the wrong kind
description: The literal is not the kind of value the type takes: a fraction where a whole number is expected, or a number where `TRUE` or `FALSE` is.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x: INT := 5.5;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed duration
description:
A `TIME` or `LTIME` literal the compiler cannot read: a unit it does not know, a missing unit, or components out of order.

A duration is written `T#1d2h3m4s5ms`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    t: TIME := T#5x;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed date
description:
A `DATE` or `LDATE` literal with a month or day that does not exist, or the wrong shape.

A date is written `D#2025-01-31`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    d: DATE := DATE#2024-13-45;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed time of day
description:
A `TOD` or `LTOD` literal with an hour, minute or second that does not exist, or the wrong shape.

A time of day is written `TOD#12:30:00.500`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    t: TOD := TOD#25:36:55.36;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed date and time
description:
A `DT` or `LDT` literal with a component that does not exist, or the wrong shape.

A date and time is written `DT#2025-01-31-12:30:00`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    dt: DT := DT#1984-06-25-25:36:55.360;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: CHAR literal of the wrong length
description: A `CHAR` holds exactly one character. The literal has none, or more than one.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    c: CHAR := CHAR#'ab';
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: STRING literal over its capacity
description:
The literal is longer than the `STRING[n]` it fills: a variable, a field's default, an element of an initializer, an input argument, the result or a store through `^`.

Widen the declaration or shorten the literal. Nothing is truncated silently.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    s: STRING[2] := 'hello';
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: STRING length not constant
description: The `n` of `STRING[n]` sizes the variable, so it has to be a compile-time constant. A named CONSTANT is accepted, as for an array bound.

title: FUNCTION used as a type
description: A FUNCTION cannot serve as the type of a variable.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    fn1 := 0;
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : fn1;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Type name used as a value
description: A type name is not a value, and neither is the name of a FUNCTION or METHOD outside its own body. Call the FUNCTION instead.
sources:
TYPE b1 : INT
END_TYPE

FUNCTION fn1
    VAR_OUTPUT
        param1: INT;
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    fn1(param1 => b1);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Assignment to a FUNCTION or METHOD
description:
A FUNCTION or METHOD has no storage. Inside its own body its name is its return value, and nowhere else is there anything to assign.

Call it, and assign what the call returns to a variable.

title: Assignment to a missing return value
description:
Inside a FUNCTION or METHOD, its own name is its return value. One declared without a return type has no return value to assign.

Declare a return type, or remove the assignment.

title: Negative STRING length
description:
The `n` of `STRING[n]` is a byte count: it cannot be negative.

Constant arithmetic wraps at its type: `STRING[200 * 200]` is an INT product, -25536. Write `DINT#200 * 200` to compute it in DINT.

title: Initial value not constant
description:
A TYPE default, a member default, a PROGRAM field and a VAR_GLOBAL are set before the program runs: their value is a constant. A named CONSTANT is accepted.

An input's default is a constant as well: the caller passes it for an omitted argument, before the callee's variables exist. A FUNCTION's or METHOD's locals start again at every call and may compute theirs.

A CONSTANT has one value for every instance and every call: a `REF()` in it names a global.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb
VAR
    m : DINT := some_global;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL
    some_global : DINT := 5;
END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : Dummy;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

PROGRAM Dummy
VAR t : INT; END_VAR
    t := 0;
END_PROGRAM

title: Function call in a repeat count
description:
The repeat count of an array initializer, `[3(x)]`, has to be a constant, and a call is not one.

Elsewhere in an initializer, a call is refused with E0401 where a constant is required, and accepted in the locals of a FUNCTION or METHOD.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    ml : ARRAY [0..2] OF INT := [1(call(IN := 5, OUT => OUT))];
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Elementary type initialized with parentheses
description: An elementary type such as INT, BOOL or REAL has no fields, so it cannot be initialized with `()`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : INT := ();
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Write to a constant
description:
A constant keeps the value it is declared with.

No assignment, output binding, `FOR` counter or bit access writes it, nor a field or an element of it. It cannot be passed to a `VAR_IN_OUT` or to `REF()` either: both could change it.

A FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS instance cannot be CONSTANT: it changes when it runs.

title: Initializer for a member that takes none
description:
An instance initializer, `d : Drive := (k := 4)`, sets the members that hold a value of their own.

A VAR_IN_OUT is given in the call, a VAR_TEMP or a CONSTANT in its declaration, a VAR_EXTERNAL on its global.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Drive
VAR_IN_OUT io : INT; END_VAR
VAR k : INT; END_VAR
    k := io;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

PROGRAM P
VAR d : Drive := (io := 30); END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Read before initialization
description:
An initial value of a FUNCTION or METHOD reads a variable declared after it, or itself.

The variables take their values at each call, in declaration order, so the read sees 0. Declare the variable it reads first.

An input, a CONSTANT and a `REF()` can be named in any order.

title: Aggregate default on a FUNCTION or METHOD input
description:
An input of a FUNCTION or METHOD keeps nothing between calls. Its default is what the caller passes when the argument is omitted, and that is a constant of an elementary type, STRING included (E0802).

A STRUCT or ARRAY initializer on such an input can never apply: a call either passes the argument or is refused. The initializer is refused where it is written.

Set the value in the body, or pass it in every call.
sources:
TYPE Pt : STRUCT x : INT; y : INT; END_STRUCT; END_TYPE

FUNCTION sum : INT
VAR_INPUT p : Pt := (x := 4, y := 5); END_VAR
    sum := p.x + p.y;
END_FUNCTION

title: Invalid array lower bound
description: The lower bound of an array dimension is not an integer constant.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[TRUE..5] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Invalid array upper bound
description: The upper bound of an array dimension is not an integer constant.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[0..TRUE] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Upper bound below the lower bound
description:
An array dimension runs from its lower bound to its upper one: the upper bound cannot be below the lower.

Equal bounds declare one element (L0212).
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[10..0] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Array index not an integer
description: A subscript has an integer type, and a subrange indexes like its base type. A BOOL, a REAL or a STRING cannot address an element.

title: Invalid repeat count
description: The repeat count of an array initializer, `[n(x)]`, is too large for an integer.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[0..2] OF INT := [99999999999999999999(0)];
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Constant index out of bounds
description: A constant subscript outside the array's bounds is refused at compile time rather than faulting the scan. Each dimension is checked.

title: Too many elements in array initializer
description: The array initializer provides more elements than the declared array size.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[0..1] OF INT := [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Index into a non-array type
description: Only an ARRAY can be indexed.

title: Array conformands not supported
description: Array conformands (`ARRAY[*]`) are not supported.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
VAR_INPUT
    x : ARRAY[*] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Incomplete subscript
description:
A multi-dimensional array is indexed in all its dimensions. `m[1]` of an `ARRAY[0..1, 0..2]` is only a part of the array, and no assignment, call or comparison takes a part.

Subscript every dimension, `m[1, 2]` or `m[1][2]`, or declare an array of an array type when a row is what the program needs.

title: ENUM base type not an integer
description: The base type of an ENUM has to be an integer type.
sources:
TYPE e1 : REAL (Red, Green, Blue)
END_TYPE

title: Not an ENUM type
description:
`#` follows a name that is not an ENUM type.

Typed literals such as `INT#16` are a separate syntax.
sources:
TYPE MyInt : INT; END_TYPE

FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    fn1 := MyInt#Red;
END_FUNCTION

title: Unknown ENUM variant
description: The referenced variant does not exist on this ENUM type.
sources:
TYPE Color : (Red, Green, Blue) END_TYPE

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    c : Color;
END_VAR
    c := Color#Yellow;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: ENUM variant value not constant
description: A variant's value is a constant: a literal, a named CONSTANT, or arithmetic over them.
sources:
FUNCTION f1 : INT
END_FUNCTION

TYPE Mode : (Idle := f1(), Run) END_TYPE

title: ENUM value outside its storage type
description:
Every value of an enum fits the type that stores it: the one written after the name, or DINT when none is.

A variant without a value is one more than the one before.
sources: TYPE Code : SINT (A := 127, B); END_TYPE

title: Subrange base type not an integer
description: The base type of a subrange has to be an integer type.
sources:
TYPE s1 : REAL (0..100)
END_TYPE

title: Value outside the subrange
description: A constant assigned to a subrange variable has to lie within its bounds.

title: Subrange bound not constant
description: The bounds of a subrange are part of the type, so each has to be a compile-time constant. A named CONSTANT and constant arithmetic are accepted, but not a variable.

title: Subrange mismatch across a reference
description: A VAR_IN_OUT argument or an output binds the caller's own variable: both sides have the same subrange, or the callee bypasses the caller's range check.

title: Subrange bounds reversed
description: A subrange holds the values from its lower bound to its upper one. Reversed, it holds none: every value stored into it is refused.
sources: TYPE Level : INT(10..1); END_TYPE

title: Wrong number of arguments
description: A call passes more or fewer arguments than the FUNCTION declares.

title: Missing required parameter
description:
A FUNCTION or METHOD call has to supply every VAR_INPUT that has no default.

A default is a constant of an elementary type, STRING included. A STRUCT or ARRAY initializer on an input is not a default, and is refused where it is written (E0407).

Name the missing parameter in the call.
sources:
FUNCTION add2 : INT
VAR_INPUT a : INT; b : INT; END_VAR
    add2 := a + b;
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION f1 : INT
    f1 := add2(a := 1);
END_FUNCTION

title: Unknown input parameter
description: The call names an input the FUNCTION does not declare.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Motor
VAR_INPUT
    u: BOOL;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    m: Motor;
END_VAR
    m(unknown := TRUE);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Unknown output parameter
description: The call names an output the FUNCTION does not declare.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
VAR_OUTPUT
    o: BOOL;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    b: BOOL;
END_VAR
    fn1(unknown => b);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Output parameter used as input
description: A positional argument lands on a VAR_OUTPUT. An output is bound by name, with `=>`.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
    VAR_INPUT
        a: INT;
    END_VAR
    VAR_OUTPUT
        b: INT;
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    fn1(1, 2);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR_IN_OUT argument not a variable
description: A VAR_IN_OUT is passed by reference. The argument is a variable, not an expression or a literal.

title: VAR_IN_OUT bound with =>
description:
The `=>` arrow binds outputs.

A VAR_IN_OUT is bound with `:=`: it flows both ways through one variable.
sources:
FUNCTION bump : INT
VAR_IN_OUT io : INT; END_VAR
    bump := io;
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION f1 : INT
VAR y : INT; END_VAR
    f1 := bump(io => y);
END_FUNCTION

title: Call of a non-callable type
description: The name called is not a FUNCTION, a METHOD or a FUNCTION_BLOCK instance.

title: Ambiguous overloaded call
description:
The call matches several overloads, none exactly.

Make it exact with a typed literal or a conversion, such as `DINT#5`.

When the overloads differ only by return type, assign the call to a variable of that type. For `NULL`, pass a variable of the reference type. When they name the parameter differently, naming it in the call picks one.

title: No matching overload
description:
No overload of this FUNCTION accepts these argument types.

The report lists each overload and what it takes.

title: Variadic parameter of a composite type
description: Only an elementary type can be variadic (`...`). A STRUCT or another composite type cannot.
sources:
TYPE MyStruct :
    STRUCT
        field1: INT;
    END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

FUNCTION sum_all : INT
    VAR_INPUT
        args: MyStruct...
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: More than one variadic parameter
description: A POU has at most one variadic parameter.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
    VAR_INPUT
        a: INT...
        b: INT...
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Variadic call without arguments
description:
A variadic parameter receives at least one argument.

A fold such as `...args+` has no value over an empty pack.
sources:
FUNCTION sum_all : INT
    VAR_INPUT
        args: INT...
    END_VAR
    sum_all := ...args+
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    fn1 := sum_all()
END_FUNCTION

title: Not a variadic parameter
description: A fold reads the variadic parameter of its own FUNCTION or METHOD. Another input, a member or an undeclared name cannot be folded.

title: Variadic parameter beside other inputs
description: A variadic parameter takes every argument of the call: it is the only `VAR_INPUT` parameter.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1 : INT
VAR_INPUT
    x: INT;
    args: INT...
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Variadic parameter used outside a fold
description:
A variadic parameter stands for as many parameters as the call passed.

Only a fold reads them: `...values+` adds them, `...values=` compares them. The parameter has no value of its own to read, write or pass on.

title: Dereference of a non-reference type
description: `^` dereferences a `REF_TO`, and a value of any other type has nothing to dereference.

title: Possibly null dereference
description:
A reference is dereferenced where it may still be NULL: it was never set since its declaration, or it was set to NULL.

Guard the dereference. `IF p <> NULL THEN` narrows `p` inside the branch, `IF p = NULL THEN RETURN; END_IF` narrows everything below, and `p := REF(x)` narrows what follows.

A `VAR_INPUT` or `VAR_IN_OUT` reference is trusted: the caller is responsible for it.

title: Reference outlives its storage
description:
A FUNCTION or METHOD returns a reference to its own local storage, and the next call reuses that storage.

Return a reference to instance state, or to a VAR_IN_OUT.
sources:
TYPE PInt : REF_TO INT; END_TYPE

FUNCTION borrow : PInt
VAR
    local : INT := 1;
END_VAR
    borrow := REF(local);
END_FUNCTION

title: Reference in RETAIN storage
description:
A RETAIN variable holds a reference, itself or in a field or member. A warm start restores the address, but a new build may have moved its target.

Keep the reference out of RETAIN, `NON_RETAIN` on a member, and set it in the first scan.

title: Access to a PRIVATE item
description: A PRIVATE variable or method is reached from its own POU only.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PRIVATE myPrivateMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Mid EXTENDS Base
    METHOD testMethod : INT
        SUPER.myPrivateMethod();
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Access to a PROTECTED item
description: A PROTECTED variable or method is reached from its own POU and those derived from it.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PROTECTED myProtectedMethod  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

FUNCTION_BLOCK fn1
    VAR
        obj: Base;
    END_VAR
    obj.myProtectedMethod();
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Access to an INTERNAL item
description: An INTERNAL variable or method is reached from its own namespace only.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    CLASS Base
        METHOD INTERNAL myInternalMethod : INT  END_METHOD
    END_CLASS
END_NAMESPACE

NAMESPACE ns2
    USING ns1;

    CLASS Mid EXTENDS Base
        METHOD testMethod : INT
            SUPER.myInternalMethod();
        END_METHOD
    END_CLASS
END_NAMESPACE

title: Access to an INTERNAL namespace
description:
A NAMESPACE INTERNAL is reachable only from inside the namespace that holds it, in the same library.

At the top level, INTERNAL means this library only.
sources:
NAMESPACE Lib
    NAMESPACE INTERNAL Impl
        FUNCTION hidden : INT
            hidden := 1;
        END_FUNCTION
    END_NAMESPACE
END_NAMESPACE

FUNCTION use : INT
    use := Lib.Impl.hidden();
END_FUNCTION

title: Call of a PRIVATE function
description:
A FUNCTION declared PRIVATE is callable only from its own namespace, nested namespaces included, on its own side of the library line.

This is an extension: the standard gives a FUNCTION no access specifier.
sources:
NAMESPACE Lib
    FUNCTION PRIVATE helper : INT
        helper := 1;
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

NAMESPACE App
    FUNCTION use : INT
        use := Lib.helper();
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

title: Specifier not applicable to a FUNCTION
description: Only PRIVATE applies to a FUNCTION (PUBLIC just spells out the default). PROTECTED and INTERNAL do not apply.

title: Access to a test-only item
description:
A `{test}` FUNCTION is the test runner's entry point, not a callable.

Code shared between tests goes in a FUNCTION without the pragma.

title: More than one EXTENDS clause
description: A CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK has a single `EXTENDS` clause.
sources:
CLASS c1 EXTENDS c2 EXTENDS c3
END_CLASS

CLASS c2
END_CLASS

CLASS c3
END_CLASS

title: More than one IMPLEMENTS clause
description: A CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK has a single `IMPLEMENTS` clause. List every interface in it: `IMPLEMENTS a, b`.
sources:
INTERFACE a
END_INTERFACE

INTERFACE b
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK fn IMPLEMENTS a IMPLEMENTS b
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: IMPLEMENTS before EXTENDS
description: The `EXTENDS` clause comes before `IMPLEMENTS`.
sources:
CLASS b
END_CLASS

FUNCTION_BLOCK fn IMPLEMENTS a EXTENDS b
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: FINAL type extended
description: A FINAL CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK cannot be extended.
sources:
CLASS FINAL Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT  myMethod := 1; END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
END_CLASS

title: THIS in a FUNCTION
description: `THIS` names the instance a METHOD or a FUNCTION_BLOCK body runs on, and a FUNCTION has no instance.

title: SUPER in a FUNCTION or PROGRAM
description: `SUPER` names the base of a FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS, and a FUNCTION or a PROGRAM has no base. In a FUNCTION_BLOCK, CLASS or METHOD without an EXTENDS clause the error is E1107.

title: SUPER without an EXTENDS clause
description: The FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS has no `EXTENDS` clause, so there is no base for `SUPER` to name.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    SUPER.method1()
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: SUPER() outside a function block body
description: `SUPER()` runs the body of the base FUNCTION_BLOCK, so it can only appear in a FUNCTION_BLOCK body. A CLASS method has no base body to run.
sources:
CLASS fb1
    METHOD method1
        SUPER()
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: SUPER() called in a method
description: `SUPER()` runs the body of the base FUNCTION_BLOCK, and only the FUNCTION_BLOCK body calls it. A method reaches the base's methods with `SUPER.Method()`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
    METHOD m1
        SUPER()
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: SUPER() called more than once
description: `SUPER()` is called at most once in a FUNCTION_BLOCK body.

title: SUPER() called inside a loop
description: `SUPER()` cannot be called inside a loop (`FOR`, `WHILE`, `REPEAT`).
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
    VAR i : INT; END_VAR
    FOR i := 1 TO 3 DO
        SUPER();
    END_FOR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Missing OVERRIDE keyword
description: A method that redefines one of its base CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK is marked OVERRIDE.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: OVERRIDE without a base method
description: A method marked OVERRIDE redefines a method of its base CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK, and the base has none of that name.
sources:
CLASS Base
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC OVERRIDE myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: FINAL method overridden
description: A FINAL method cannot be overridden in a derived CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC FINAL myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC OVERRIDE myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Inherited variable redeclared
description: A derived FUNCTION_BLOCK cannot redeclare a variable it inherits from its base: the names are unique across both.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
VAR c : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
VAR c : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Missing ABSTRACT method implementation
description: A concrete CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK implements every ABSTRACT method of its base.
sources:
CLASS ABSTRACT Base
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
END_CLASS

title: ABSTRACT method in a concrete POU
description: A CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK that declares an ABSTRACT method is ABSTRACT itself.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Instantiation of an ABSTRACT type
description: An ABSTRACT CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK has no implementation of its own, so it cannot be instantiated. Declare a variable of a derived type instead.
sources:
CLASS ABSTRACT Base
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

PROGRAM Main
VAR
    b : Base;
END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Unimplemented interface method
description: A CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK that implements an INTERFACE declares every method of it.
sources:
INTERFACE IMyInterface
    METHOD myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS MyClass IMPLEMENTS IMyInterface
END_CLASS

title: Access specifier on interface method prototype
description: An interface method prototype takes no access specifier: interface methods are always PUBLIC.
sources:
INTERFACE iface
    METHOD PUBLIC m1
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

title: Interface type outside a parameter
description:
An interface type is a `VAR_INPUT` or `VAR_IN_OUT` parameter of a FUNCTION or METHOD, passed by reference: the caller's type replaces it and its methods run on the caller's instance.

It cannot be a variable, a member, an output, a global, or an input of a FUNCTION_BLOCK: an instance would store it across calls.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

PROGRAM Main
    VAR
        dev : ITF1;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Interface as a return type
description: An interface is not a return type: the concrete type would flow from callee to caller, unknown at compile time.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION Make : ITF1
END_FUNCTION

title: Interface nested in an aggregate
description: An interface cannot be inside an ARRAY, a REF_TO or a STRUCT: the aggregate would store values of different types.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

PROGRAM Main
    VAR
        arr : ARRAY[0..2] OF ITF1;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Assignment to an interface parameter
description: An interface parameter, `VAR_INPUT` or `VAR_IN_OUT`, stays bound to what the caller passed and cannot be assigned. Call its methods, or pass it on.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK Impl IMPLEMENTS ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION Use : INT
    VAR_IN_OUT dev : ITF1; END_VAR
    VAR other : Impl; END_VAR
    dev := other;
END_FUNCTION

title: Method parameter count mismatch
description:
A method declares another number of parameters than the method it implements or overrides.

Parameters are matched by position.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC OVERRIDE myMethod : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; b : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method parameter type mismatch
description:
A parameter has another type than the one at the same position in the method it implements or overrides.

No widening applies.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : REAL; END_VAR
        M := 0;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method return type mismatch
description: A method returns another type than the method it implements or overrides, or returns one where that method does not.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : REAL
        M := 0.0;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method parameter name mismatch
description: A parameter has another name than the one at the same position in the method it implements or overrides. A call by name would reach another parameter.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT b : INT; END_VAR
        M := b;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method parameter section mismatch
description:
A parameter is in another section (VAR_INPUT, VAR_OUTPUT, VAR_IN_OUT) than in the method it implements or overrides.

The section decides how the argument is passed.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_IN_OUT a : INT; END_VAR
        M := a;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Base of the wrong kind
description:
`EXTENDS` on a FUNCTION_BLOCK names a FUNCTION_BLOCK or a CLASS.

`EXTENDS` on a CLASS names a CLASS: a CLASS has no body to inherit a FUNCTION_BLOCK's.

`IMPLEMENTS`, and `EXTENDS` on an INTERFACE, name INTERFACEs.
sources:
INTERFACE IDrive
    METHOD start : BOOL END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK Motor EXTENDS IDrive
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Method parameter default mismatch
description:
An input has another default than in the method it implements or overrides.

A call passes the default of the method it names. Through the base, or through an INTERFACE, the implementation's own default would not apply: give both the same default.
sources:
INTERFACE IScale
    METHOD Scale : INT
        VAR_INPUT k : INT := 1; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK Doubler IMPLEMENTS IScale
    METHOD PUBLIC Scale : INT
        VAR_INPUT k : INT := 2; END_VAR
        Scale := k * 10;
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: SUPER() with a CLASS base
description: `SUPER()` runs the body of the base FUNCTION_BLOCK. A FUNCTION_BLOCK may extend a CLASS, but a CLASS has no body. Its methods are reached with `SUPER.Method()`.
sources:
CLASS Counter
    VAR n : INT; END_VAR
END_CLASS

FUNCTION_BLOCK Ticker EXTENDS Counter
    SUPER();
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: SUPER calls a method with no body
description:
`SUPER.Method()` runs the base's own method.

An ABSTRACT one has no body to run, nor does one the base takes from an INTERFACE without implementing it.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK ABSTRACT Shape
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT Area : INT
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK Square EXTENDS Shape
    METHOD PUBLIC OVERRIDE Area : INT
        Area := SUPER.Area() + 4;
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: ABSTRACT method with a body
description: An ABSTRACT method is implemented by the blocks that derive from its own, so statements in it would never run. Remove ABSTRACT to give the method its body here.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK ABSTRACT Shape
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT Area : INT
        Area := 5;
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Interface method implemented without PUBLIC
description:
The method that implements an INTERFACE's is public, as the interface's are: a call through the interface reaches it from anywhere.

Write `PUBLIC` or no specifier. `PRIVATE`, `PROTECTED` and `INTERNAL` are refused.
sources:
INTERFACE IShow
    METHOD Show : INT END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK Pump IMPLEMENTS IShow
    METHOD PRIVATE Show : INT
        Show := 7;
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: EXIT outside loop
description: `EXIT` leaves a loop: FOR, WHILE or REPEAT. Outside one there is nothing to leave.

title: CONTINUE outside loop
description: `CONTINUE` goes to the next round of a loop: FOR, WHILE or REPEAT. Outside one there is no next round.

title: FOR control not a variable
description:
A FOR statement's control is a bare variable name.

A struct field, an array element, a dereference or a bit access cannot be a loop counter.

title: FOR step not a nonzero constant
description: The step sets the loop's direction at compile time, so it has to be a nonzero constant. A named CONSTANT and arithmetic over constants are accepted.

title: CASE label not constant
description: A CASE label is a constant: a literal, a string, an enum value, a named CONSTANT, or arithmetic over them.

title: FOR counter not an integer
description:
A FOR loop counts in an integer: SINT, INT, DINT, LINT, an unsigned one of those, or a subrange or alias of one.

A BOOL, a REAL, a TIME, a bit string such as BYTE, or an enumeration is not a counter.

title: CASE selector of the wrong type
description:
`CASE` branches on an integer, a bit string, a CHAR, an enum or a STRING.

A REAL, a duration or a date is branched on with `IF`. So is a BOOL.

title: Empty CASE range
description: A range runs from its lower bound to its upper one. Reversed, it holds no value and its arm never runs.

title: Type contains itself
description:
A type contains a member of its own type by value: a STRUCT with a field of its own type, or a FUNCTION_BLOCK with an instance of itself. Such a type would have no finite size.

A member held by address, a REF_TO, is no part of the type and makes no cycle.
sources:
TYPE s1 : STRUCT
    field1 : s1;
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

title: Types contain each other
description:
Two or more types contain each other by value, around a cycle, so none of them has a finite size.

A member held by address, a VAR_IN_OUT or a REF_TO, is no part of the type and makes no cycle.
sources:
TYPE a : STRUCT
    field1 : b;
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

TYPE b : STRUCT
    field1 : a;
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

title: No project configuration
description:
The workspace has no config.toml, so its files are checked as loose sources: no library is loaded and nothing is compiled.

Add a config.toml with a [project] table, or point --workspace at the directory that has one.

title: More than one CONFIGURATION
description: A workspace holds a single CONFIGURATION. Describe another PLC in its own workspace.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION cfg1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

CONFIGURATION cfg2
    RESOURCE res2 ON CPU
        TASK t2(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst2 WITH t2 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: More than one RESOURCE
description: A configuration holds a single RESOURCE, since the runtime scans on one thread.

title: TASK or PROGRAM outside a RESOURCE
description: A CONFIGURATION contains RESOURCE blocks, and the tasks and the programs bound to them are declared inside one: `RESOURCE <name> ON <cpu> ... END_RESOURCE`.

title: Missing PRIORITY in TASK
description: A TASK declares its PRIORITY.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#20ms);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unusable TASK priority
description: A TASK's `PRIORITY` is a 32-bit unsigned integer, 0 the most urgent.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION cfg1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 99999999999);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: INTERVAL after PRIORITY in TASK
description: In a TASK, INTERVAL comes before PRIORITY.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(PRIORITY := 1, INTERVAL := T#20ms);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: SINGLE after INTERVAL in TASK
description: In a TASK, SINGLE comes before INTERVAL.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#20ms, SINGLE := var1, PRIORITY := 1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: SINGLE after PRIORITY in TASK
description: In a TASK, SINGLE comes before PRIORITY.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(PRIORITY := 1, SINGLE := var1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unschedulable TASK
description: A TASK is scheduled by a cyclic INTERVAL. SINGLE (event-driven) tasks are not supported by the scan dispatcher.

title: Unknown TASK reference
description: The task name referenced in a `WITH` clause does not exist in this configuration.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH unknown_task : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Program instance without a task
description: Every program instance in a RESOURCE is attached to a TASK with `WITH`, and an unattached instance is never scheduled.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR n : INT; END_VAR
    n := n + 1;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        PROGRAM P1 : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unknown instance in VAR_CONFIG
description: A `VAR_CONFIG` path references a program instance that does not exist.
sources:
PROGRAM MyProg
    VAR
        x : INT;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : MyProg;
    END_RESOURCE

    VAR_CONFIG
        noSuchInst.x : INT := 42;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unknown field in VAR_CONFIG
description: A `VAR_CONFIG` path references a field that does not exist on the resolved type.
sources:
PROGRAM MyProg
    VAR
        x : INT;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : MyProg;
    END_RESOURCE

    VAR_CONFIG
        inst1.nonexistent : INT := 42;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: VAR_ACCESS type mismatch
description: A `VAR_ACCESS` declaration's type does not match the referenced variable's actual type.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
VAR
    my_var : INT;
END_VAR
VAR_ACCESS
    accessor : my_var : BOOL;
END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH task1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Address not locatable
description:
A variable of a FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS takes no complete address. In a block, declare it `AT %I*` and locate each instance in `VAR_CONFIG`. Elsewhere, declare it in a PROGRAM or a VAR_GLOBAL.

A STRUCT field takes no address: it is part of every variable of its type. Declare the channel in a FUNCTION_BLOCK instead, where `VAR_CONFIG` locates it per instance.

A partial address like `%I*` goes on a variable of a PROGRAM, FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS, and names its area alone.

An address names its area with `I`, `Q` or `M` and its width with `X`, `B`, `W`, `D` or `L`. A library names no complete address.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Valve
VAR
    POS AT %QW28 : INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Unknown multibit access size
description: A partial access names its width with `X`, `B`, `W`, `D` or `L`, in either case.

title: Write to an input location
description:
The host writes the inputs before every scan: a program reads `%I` and cannot write it, nor give it an initial value.

`%Q` and `%M` can be written.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR_EXTERNAL sensor : BOOL; END_VAR
    sensor := TRUE;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL sensor AT %IX0.0 : BOOL; END_VAR
    RESOURCE R ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: RETAIN on an I/O location
description:
Only `%M` can be `RETAIN`: a restored `%I` or `%Q` would run the first scan on the last power cycle's values.

A variable declared `AT %M*` has no storage of its own: to persist a marker, locate it in full.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR_EXTERNAL sensor : BOOL; END_VAR
VAR seen : BOOL; END_VAR
    seen := sensor;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL RETAIN sensor AT %IX0.0 : BOOL; END_VAR
    RESOURCE R ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Duplicate location
description:
Two declarations are bound to the same address.

Declare the address once and name that variable.

title: Location type mismatch
description:
A located variable is an elementary type as wide as its address: `%IW` takes a WORD, an INT or a UINT, and `%ID` a DWORD, a DINT or a REAL.

An enum, a subrange, an ARRAY, a STRUCT or a STRING is refused.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR_EXTERNAL wide : INT; END_VAR
VAR t : INT; END_VAR
    t := wide;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL wide AT %IX0.0 : INT; END_VAR
    RESOURCE R ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Part of a wider address
description:
An address inside a wider one the program also names is part of it, with no storage of its own: beside a `%QW0`, `%QX0.3` is its bit 3.

A bit cannot be passed to a VAR_IN_OUT or referenced, and no part can be RETAIN or have an initial value.

title: Location refused
description:
A `VAR_CONFIG` entry with `AT` locates a variable declared `AT %I*`, `%Q*` or `%M*`, in one instance.

The address is complete, in the variable's area and as wide as its type, not a bit of a wider address, and given once.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR level : INT; END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_CONFIG
    Res.P1.level AT %IW2 : INT;
END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Variable not located
description:
Each instance of a variable declared `AT %I*`, `%Q*` or `%M*` needs its address in `VAR_CONFIG`, by a path such as `Res.P1.d.level`.

Hold the instance in a PROGRAM, or in a function block the PROGRAM holds: an array element, a STRUCT field, a global, a VAR_TEMP, a VAR_INPUT or a function's variable has no such path.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Drive
VAR
    level AT %I* : INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

PROGRAM P
VAR d : Drive; END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Configuration entry refused
description:
A `VAR_CONFIG` entry names a variable by its path from a PROGRAM instance and repeats its type: `Res.P1.d.level : INT := 5;`.

The path names instances and variables only, and each variable gets one entry.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR level AT %I* : INT; END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_CONFIG
    Res.P1.level AT %IW2 : UINT;
END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Located variable overwritten
description:
A variable declared `AT %I*`, `%Q*` or `%M*` points at the address `VAR_CONFIG` gives it. An instance initializer cannot set it: give its starting value in the `VAR_CONFIG` entry.

A copy of the instance, `b := a` or `fb(o => b)`, would write the other instance's address over it. Copy the other members one by one.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Drive
VAR out AT %Q* : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

PROGRAM P
VAR d : Drive := (out := 30); END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_CONFIG
    Res.P1.d.out AT %QW0 : INT;
END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Program configuration element refused
description:
An element of a program's list, like `F(x1 := %IX0.0, y1 => total, fb1 WITH FAST)`, is refused.

`:=` feeds an input from a global of the same type, an address as wide or a constant, and `=>` copies an output to a global or an address. `fb WITH task` names a function block instance of the program and a task of the resource.
sources:
PROGRAM F
VAR_INPUT x1 : BOOL; END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT y1 : INT; END_VAR
    IF x1 THEN y1 := y1 + 1; END_IF;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : F(y1 := 1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Partial access out of range
description:
A partial access names a part of its base: bit 0 to 15 of a WORD with `%X`, byte 0 or 1 with `%B`.

An offset past the last part, or a part wider than the base, is refused.

title: Extern pragma outside a FUNCTION
description:
Only a FUNCTION can be `{extern}`.

Wrap the import in a FUNCTION and call it from the block.
sources:
{extern 'host' 'fb-extern'}
FUNCTION_BLOCK Modbus
VAR_INPUT n : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Not representable on an extern FUNCTION
description:
An `{extern}` FUNCTION is a WASM import: its VAR_INPUT are the params, its scalar VAR_OUTPUT and return value the results.

It cannot have a VAR_IN_OUT, an aggregate or STRING output, or a body.
sources:
{extern 'host' 'fill'}
FUNCTION fill : INT
VAR_IN_OUT buf : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Test pragma outside a FUNCTION
description:
`{test}` is valid only on a FUNCTION.

A POU that only tests use is hidden with FUNCTION PRIVATE.

title: Wasm pragma outside a FUNCTION
description: A `{wasm}` intrinsic is only read in a FUNCTION body. Anywhere else the pragma would have no effect.

title: Unknown wasm instruction
description: The instruction this `{wasm}` pragma names is not one the compiler knows.

title: Wasm operand not declared
description: Each operand of a `{wasm}` statement, and its (result), has to be a parameter, a local or the return value of the FUNCTION.

title: Wasm operands of the wrong type
description:
The operands of a `{wasm}` pragma do not match the instruction's signature.

The message shows what the instruction takes and what it is given.

title: Export pragma outside a FUNCTION
description: `{export}` is valid only on a FUNCTION. A PROGRAM is already exported, and a FUNCTION_BLOCK or METHOD needs an instance to run on: wrap the call in a FUNCTION and export that.
sources:
{export}
FUNCTION_BLOCK Motor
VAR_INPUT run : BOOL; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: FUNCTION not exportable
description:
An `{export}` FUNCTION is exported under its one name: it cannot be `{extern}`, `{test}`, variadic, overloaded, or take an interface.

It cannot take a name the module exports itself: `__init`, `memory`, the base and the size of each memory band. Neither can a `{test}`, exported in a debug build.

Export a plain FUNCTION that calls it.

title: Unknown pragma
description:
rk knows eight pragmas: `{test}`, `{once}`, `{export}`, `{warn}`, `{info}`, `{allow}`, `{extern}` and `{wasm}`. Any other text in braces is refused, wherever it stands.

An attribute copied from another toolchain is not ignored, because some of them change what the code means. Remove it, or write in rk what it was for.

title: {info} notice
description: A call targets a POU annotated `{info = '...'}`: the notice is shown at the call site.
sources:
{info = 'prefer new_fn for better performance'}
FUNCTION old_fn : INT
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION caller : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    x := old_fn();
END_FUNCTION

title: {warn} notice
description: A call targets a POU annotated `{warn = '...'}`: the warning, a deprecation for instance, is shown at the call site.
sources:
{warn = 'this function is deprecated, use fn2 instead'}
FUNCTION fn1 : INT
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION caller : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    x := fn1();
END_FUNCTION

title: Pragma without effect on the POU
description:
A pragma has no meaning on this kind of POU: `{once}` on a PROGRAM.

A misplaced `{test}` or `{extern}` is an error instead (E1503, E1501).

title: {once} POU called more than once
description: A POU marked `{once}` is called more than once in the same body. `{once}` means one call per execution cycle.

title: Unknown rule name in {allow}
description: An `{allow 'rule-name'}` pragma names a lint rule that does not exist, so it silences nothing. Rule names are those of `[linter.rules]`, such as `input-assignment`.

title: Unreachable code
description:
A statement follows a RETURN, EXIT, CONTINUE or `__RAISE` in the same block. It never runs.

It is checked like any other statement: an unknown name or a type mismatch there is reported.

title: Division by zero
description: A division or modulo operation uses a literal zero as the divisor.

title: Constant condition
description: A condition in an IF, WHILE, or REPEAT statement is always TRUE or always FALSE.

title: Self-assignment
description: A variable is assigned to itself, which has no effect.

title: Self-comparison
description: A variable is compared to itself. The result is always TRUE or always FALSE.

title: Subtraction from self
description: Subtracting a variable from itself always results in 0.

title: Identity operation
description: An operation with an identity value has no effect (adding 0, multiplying by 1, etc.).

title: Identical subexpressions
description: Both sides of a boolean operator are the same expression, which is usually a copy-paste error.

title: Duplicate CASE value
description: Two CASE branches use the same selector value. Only the first matches.

title: FOR loop step sign mismatch
description: The sign of the FOR loop's step does not match the direction of its bounds.

title: Constant FOR loop bounds
description: A FOR loop has equal start and end bounds, so its body runs exactly once.

title: FOR control variable written
description: A FOR loop's control variable is written inside the loop body, so the loop no longer runs the declared number of times.

title: Assignment to input variable
description: A `VAR_INPUT` is assigned inside the POU body. Inputs are set by the caller.

title: Missing return assignment
description: A function or method declares a return type but never assigns the return value.

title: Variable named after its POU
description: A variable has the same name as the function block, method, or program it is declared in.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK MyFB
VAR
    MyFB : INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Method variable named after a member
description: A method's local or parameter has the name of a member of its block. This is legal, and the local wins, but the two are easy to confuse.

title: External instance mutation
description: A field of a FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS instance is written from outside the instance, which should own its data.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK MyFB
VAR
    x : INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION caller : INT
VAR
    fb : MyFB;
END_VAR
    fb.x := 42;
END_FUNCTION

title: Global accessed without VAR_EXTERNAL
description: A configuration VAR_GLOBAL is read directly by name. IEC 61131-3 imports it with VAR_EXTERNAL.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR n : INT; END_VAR
    n := gCount;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    VAR_GLOBAL gCount : INT; END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Instance in a stateless POU
description:
A FUNCTION or METHOD holds or returns a FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS instance. The instance starts over at every call, so a timer in it never expires.

Hold it in a FUNCTION_BLOCK or PROGRAM and pass it as a VAR_IN_OUT. A `{test}` FUNCTION may hold one.

title: Variable and method with the same name
description:
A variable and a method of a block, or of one it extends, have the same name. This is legal, as in CODESYS and TwinCAT, but easy to misread.

Inside the block the name is the variable, `THIS` included. From outside an instance, a variable the block keeps to itself gives way to the method.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Outer
VAR
    step : INT;
END_VAR
    METHOD STEP END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: STRING with a Latin-1 escape
description:
A STRING literal holds a `$hh` escape of $80 or more that is not part of UTF-8 text.

A `$hh` escape is one byte, but a STRING is UTF-8. Code written for Latin-1 uses `$E9` for `é`, while in UTF-8 `é` is `$C3$A9`, so `'caf$E9' = 'café'` is FALSE.

Write the character itself, or its UTF-8 bytes. A CHAR is a code point: `CHAR#'$E9'` is `é` and is not reported.

title: Recursive call
description:
A call leads back to the POU making it, directly or through other POUs. IEC 61131-3 has no recursion, and rk runs it the way CODESYS does.

A recursive POU gets a frame on the stack at each call for its arrays, strings, structures and instances. Any other POU keeps them at a fixed address and never touches the stack.

The stack holds 64 KiB, and nothing bounds the depth before the program runs: too deep a recursion stops it with `stack overflow`. A loop does the same work in a fixed amount of memory.

title: Negative radix literal
description:
An untyped radix literal has its top bit set where a signed integer is expected, so the value is negative.

A radix literal is a bit pattern of the width its context gives it: `16#80` is 128 in an INT and -128 in a SINT. Write `SINT#16#80` when the pattern is meant, or use a wider type for 128.

A typed literal is not reported. Neither is a literal under a minus, where it is a plain number (`-(16#80)` is minus 128), nor an operand of AND, OR or XOR, where its bits are the point.
sources:
FUNCTION Mask : SINT
VAR m : SINT := 16#80; END_VAR
    Mask := m;
END_FUNCTION

title: Unused variable
description: A variable is declared but never used in the body.

title: Variable named after a POU
description: A variable name shadows a POU (function, function block, class, etc.) available in scope.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK PrintLog
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Duplicate variable section
description: The same variable section (VAR, VAR_INPUT, ...) appears more than once in a POU. Merge them into one.

title: Duplicate namespace
description: The same namespace is declared more than once in the same file. Merge them into one.
sources:
NAMESPACE Utils
    FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

NAMESPACE Utils
    FUNCTION fn2 : INT
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

title: Duplicate configuration
description: CONFIGURATION blocks of the same name merge, which is how VAR_GLOBALs are split across files. Two in the same file separate nothing: merge them.
sources:
CONFIGURATION Plant
    VAR_GLOBAL
        a : INT;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

CONFIGURATION Plant
    VAR_GLOBAL
        b : INT;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Uninitialized output
description:
A `VAR_OUTPUT` is never written in the body.

It keeps its initial value: its initializer, or the default of its type (0, an enum's first value, a subrange's lower bound). That is legal, but an output the body never writes is usually unfinished.

title: Negated condition
description: An `IF NOT ... THEN ... ELSE` can be simplified by swapping the branches and removing the negation.

title: Negated comparison
description: `NOT (x = y)` can be simplified to `x <> y`, and similar for other comparison operators.

title: Boolean comparison
description: A comparison with a boolean literal can be simplified. Use the variable directly, or negate it.

title: Redundant NOT
description: A double negation (`NOT NOT x`) can be simplified to just `x`.

title: Unnecessary ELSE
description: The ELSE branch is unnecessary because all preceding IF/ELSIF branches end with RETURN, EXIT, or CONTINUE.

title: Single-element array
description: An array dimension has equal bounds: one element.

title: Explicit default FOR step
description: `BY 1` is the default step.

title: Aggregate copy
description:
An assignment or a call binding copies an ARRAY, a STRUCT or a FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS instance whole. The copy takes every element and field, nested ones included, and costs as much as the type is large. A copy in the body runs at every scan.

A STRING copies its text only and is not reported.

To share the value instead, pass it as a VAR_IN_OUT or keep a REF_TO it.

title: Unused import
description: A `USING` directive imports a namespace that is never referenced.
sources:
NAMESPACE Tools
    FUNCTION_BLOCK Logger
    END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
END_NAMESPACE

title: Unused return value
description: A function call discards its return value. Assign it to a variable when ignoring it is intended.

title: Missing input parameter
description:
A FUNCTION_BLOCK or PROGRAM call leaves out a VAR_INPUT. The input keeps its previous value.

Legal, but usually an oversight. In a FUNCTION call it is E0802.

title: CASE without ELSE
description: A CASE statement has no ELSE branch: an unlisted value runs nothing.

title: Empty body
description: A function, function block, method, or program has an empty body.
sources:
FUNCTION compute : INT
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty IF branch
description: An IF or ELSIF branch has no statements.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR
    x : BOOL;
END_VAR
    IF x THEN
    END_IF;
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty CASE branch
description: A CASE branch has no statements.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    CASE x OF
        1:
        2: test := 20;
    END_CASE;
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty loop body
description: A FOR, WHILE, or REPEAT loop has no statements in its body.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR
    i : INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i := 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty type declaration
description: A STRUCT has no fields or an ENUM has no variants.

title: Effectless statement
description: A statement has no side effects and does nothing.

title: Unnecessary parentheses
description: Parentheses around a simple variable or literal have no effect and can be removed.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    test := (x);
END_FUNCTION

title: Collapsible IF
description: Two nested IF statements without ELSE branches can be collapsed into a single `IF a AND b THEN`.

title: Literal on the left of a comparison
description: A literal is on the left side of a comparison. Swap the operands for the conventional order.
